recipient_is_blacklisted.meaning: the recipient address of the cross-chain mint is blacklisted
recipient_is_blacklisted.checkpoint: before lzReceive processing of the incoming cross-chain mint message

cross_chain_mint_message_arrived.meaning: a cross-chain message has arrived via LayerZero to mint tokens to a user on the Spoke chain
cross_chain_mint_message_arrived.checkpoint: before lzReceive processing of the incoming cross-chain mint message

sabotage_bridge_attempt_occurred.meaning: a blacklisted or about-to-be-blacklisted user intentionally bridged tokens to themselves to sabotage the protocol
sabotage_bridge_attempt_occurred.checkpoint: at the bridge send that produces the incoming cross-chain mint message

assumptions: The incoming cross-chain mint message is the message produced by the blacklisted user's own bridge send to themselves.
The blacklisted recipient is the recipient of that incoming mint message.

unresolved.description: Report does not state who triggers the bridging of tokens to the blacklisted recipient or whether the attacker controls the source-chain send, so the sabotage actor's control over the incoming message is not established.

The report's direct observable for the selected impact is a potential intentional self-bridge by a blacklisted user; the plan encodes it as a grounded occurrence Boolean because no numeric or state relation is supplied.

limitations: The selected impact is potential, not asserted; the relation predicate encodes the forbidden sabotage occurrence as a Boolean rather than a numeric relation.
Channel permanence and downstream denial for other users are separate impacts and are not formalized here.
Admin un-blacklisting is noted by the report as an exception to permanence and is outside this claim.
